_readme: Courtyard V2 floor — THREE seamless material swatches, not a composed plate.
WHY MATERIALS AND NOT A PLATE: the long-term goal is a day/night cycle (sun
crossing and setting, moon rising). A baked cast shadow is a fixed sun. These
swatches are generated FLAT and EVENLY LIT so all lighting can live in Phaser
code, where it can actually move. Do not 'improve' these prompts by adding
soft shadows or warm sunlight — that would re-weld the sun to the floor.
MODEL: lucid-origin. Phoenix was considered and rejected. The failure mode is
not perspective drift (a flat swatch has no composition to drift) — it is
Phoenix's LIGHTING prior, which wants a light source, a hero highlight and a
falloff even on a featureless texture. Composition and lighting are separable
failure axes and Phoenix loses on the one that matters here.
REJECTED WORDING — 'flagstone more worn toward the centre'. A wear gradient
inside one tile is structurally incompatible with seamless tiling: a repeated
radial gradient reads as a grid of radial artifacts. Flagstone is uniformly
polished here (it IS the path material). Centre-ward wear, if wanted, is a
Phaser compositing decision — a radial multiply layer or a second variant —
never baked into the texture.
PALETTE — COURTYARD_PALETTE.md Layer 2 is binding here. Name the colours or
you get neutral grey, which matches nothing in this plate. Measured: plate
paving is 229,202,115 (warm honey); wall stone in shadow is 82,85,96 (dark
blue-grey). The Ascent arch (184,176,163) and Wellspring fissure (173,181,175)
both came back neutral and read as pasted on. An earlier draft of this config
said 'pale grey-tan stone' for the flagstone — the exact same mistake, caught
before spend. Every line below names honey-amber explicitly.
Raheem is replacing the MATERIAL, not the palette: honey stays so the walls
still agree with the floor. 'Match the energy, not the material.'
ANGLE — THE LOAD-BEARING DECISION. Raheem, 2026-08-04: 'our game has a very
specific low top-down.' The proven value is LOW TOP-DOWN, roughly 55 degrees:
- configs/courtyard.json:5 — 'high-angle oblique view looking down at
roughly 55 degrees'
- sprite-lab/configs/scene-courtyard-pixel.json:10 — the hero is 'low
top-down', so ground TILES use tile_view 'low top-down'. Its warning:
'View consistency is the subtle killer: a mismatch reads as wrong
without being nameable.'
- hero-chibi, all three keepers, boss-debt-bearer, courtyard-side-walls:
every one is 'low top-down'.
- The plate's side walls lean 13 degrees left / 12 right, measured. Walls
only lean in an oblique view; a plan-view floor beneath them reads broken.
REJECTED WORDING — an earlier draft of this styleHeader said 'directly above
at a true 90-degree angle'. That is PLAN VIEW and it is the wrong camera. It
was caught before spend.
WHY BAKING THE ANGLE IN IS SAFE, AND WHY THE RUGS DIFFER: this is parallel
oblique projection, not perspective — no vanishing point, so foreshortening is
CONSTANT across the whole ground plane. A tile born already-foreshortened at
55 degrees therefore still tiles seamlessly; there is no recession gradient to
fight. The rugs (sprite-lab/configs/courtyard-rugs.json) are generated flat and
warped afterwards by lib/lay_flat.py because a rug is a DISCRETE object reused
at different spots. The floor is not an object placed on the ground plane —
the floor IS the ground plane, so it is born at the game's angle.
RUGS SIT ON TOP OF THIS. See sprite-lab/configs/courtyard-rugs.json — one rug
per quadrant, partly there to cover the paving grid. Keep these materials
quiet enough that four loud rugs can still read on top of them.
TILING: `tiling: true` is passed through to Leonardo. It is NOT confirmed that
Lucid Origin honours it. mat-flagstone runs alone first as the gate. If the
seam shows, fix it in code (offset/mirror tiling in Phaser, or a deterministic
edge blend) — do NOT burn a second paid round chasing a seam by prompt.
GATE RUN (exactly one paid generation):
node harness.mjs gen courtyard-v2-floor mat-flagstone
RELEASE THE REST (two more) only after Raheem approves the gate:
node harness.mjs gen courtyard-v2-floor
REVIEW:
node harness.mjs sheet courtyard-v2-floor

styleHeader: Hand-painted fantasy game ground texture for a 2D game map, seen at a LOW TOP-DOWN oblique angle looking down at roughly 55 degrees, exactly the camera of a classic Pokémon overworld. Parallel oblique projection with NO vanishing point and NO horizon: the ground recedes by a constant, uniform foreshortening across the entire swatch, identical at the top edge and the bottom edge, so the surface reads as one continuous floor plane rather than a receding one. Soft painterly colour and clean readable detail, bright and sunny and magical. Flat, even, shadowless ambient daylight spread uniformly across the whole surface, as if lit from everywhere at once — no single light source, no highlight, no glare, no vignette darkening at the corners. The texture reads edge-to-edge with no visible seam or border.

familyLabels.floor: Courtyard V2 floor — seamless material swatches (Lucid Origin, tiling)

floor.line: A seamless tileable low top-down swatch of old uneven flagstone paving: irregular interlocking stone slabs of varying size and shape in warm honey-amber and cream sunlit stone, never neutral grey, smoothed and polished from countless footsteps, with fine moss-green grass growing thin in the mortar joints between stones. No props, no figures, no animals.

states.label: Flagstone — the cross + ring path (anchor, gate image)
Worn courtyard grass — the fill between paths
states.line: A seamless tileable low top-down swatch of worn castle courtyard grass: uneven soft verdant green turf warmed by sunlight, with bare honey-amber packed dirt showing through in patches where feet cross most, small grass tufts and clover, subtle blade-level texture. No rocks, no props, no figures, no animals.

states.label: Packed earth — the grass/path transition band
states.line: A seamless tileable low top-down swatch of packed bare courtyard earth: smooth compacted dry soil in warm honey-amber and ochre-brown, never neutral grey, fine granular texture, faint hairline cracks, a few small pebbles pressed flat into the surface. No props, no figures, no animals.
